Unable to reach consensus.

Considering this is your proposal and essentially nobody uses phosphor-power except for IBM, you're not likely to get very much useful feedback on this.  You've essentially created an IBM-only "playground" in phosphor-power now.
Noted. I encourage the community to use phosphor-power apps.

In the last few years there has been a shift to move system-specific configuration files into the same repo that contains the code (such as EM).  Would it make sense to put the JSON file in a subdirectory within phosphor-power?  That is where the other JSON files are for the phosphor-power apps.
Updated.

In the phosphor-power repository, the current service files are named to match the application, such as `phosphor-regulators.service`.  It is not a hard requirement, but it would be more consistent to name it `phosphor-chassis-power.service`.
Updated.

This is a pretty non-useful statement.  What is interesting is what repositories _are_ going to be affected in order to support your new feature.  I assume this is going to have impact to other repositories, so you need to enumerate them.
Updated - slight change in design; no impacts to other repos to support the new feature.

From the discussion earlier in this document, maybe tests like the following would be good too?
* Test where some chassis are removed (not present)
* Test where power cable is removed from all PSUs
* Test where cabling / hardware that connects the BMC to a non-BMC chassis is not working (if relevant given hardware design).
Updated.
I'm not sure what this means.  If this app is not necessarily providing them, then is it a requirement?

Just wanted to document the slight change in direction that chassis input power interfaces were being provided by other apps, not by this app (eg chassis-state-manager CurrentPowerStatus, phosphor-power PowerSystemInputs)
Done

I think to have any chance of others taking advantage of this new app, the devil will be in the details of this file and how generic it can be. But as noted by Patrick, it's really only IBM at this point. But it should definitely a goal to make this generic enough that other could some day make use of it. The general use case of monitoring other chassis's for power issues and handling that seems like a fairly universal one.

Are you planning on supporting a test directory that is writable and overrides the standard directory?

If not, you can probably remove the "Standard directory: " wording here.
Not at this time; I'll remove.
Done

For other D-Bus paths related to chassis, chassis 0 represents the entire system.  Chassis 1 is the first chassis.

Will `/xyz/openbmc_project/power/chassis/chassis0` represent the entire system?  If not, should numbering start at 1 instead to be consistent?  Otherwise other apps will have to convert between 1-based numbering and 0-based numbering.
Good catch, there is no reason to have a system indicator since it would be dead; I'll update.
Done
